wizard.title: Get started
wizard.lead: Connect your accounts once. Then every repository becomes a project in a few minutes.

subscription.title: Subscribe to bohr.io Cloud
subscription.text: bohr.io Cloud is bohr ready to use, with nothing to install. To create projects here, you need a subscription.
subscription.point1: bohr runs and maintains the instance for you, with this panel and the Telegram bot.
subscription.point2: Your sites are published to your own Cloudflare account, which you connect in the next step.
subscription.point3: Infrastructure is paid directly to the providers: Cloudflare (the free plan is enough) and Anthropic tokens.
subscription.confirming: Payment received. We are confirming the subscription with Stripe…
subscription.paid: Subscription active! Let's continue the setup.
subscription.notConfirmed: We have not received the payment confirmation yet. Wait a moment and check again.

cloudflare.title: Connect your Cloudflare account
cloudflare.text: Your projects' sites and their domains are published to your Cloudflare account. Any plan works, including the free one.
cloudflare.step1: Open the token template on Cloudflare. The main permissions come filled in.
cloudflare.step2: Create the token, copy it and paste it here.
cloudflare.agentNote: The agent's sandbox is a Container. With the Workers Paid plan, also add the {permission} permission to the token (the link cannot fill it in) and it runs in your own account.
cloudflare.tokenHint: The instance keeps the token encrypted and only uses it to create and update your projects' Workers.
cloudflare.invalidFormat: That does not look like a Cloudflare API token. Copy the whole token, without spaces.
cloudflare.missingHint: Edit the token on Cloudflare (or create another one from the template), add what is missing and paste it again.

capabilities.durable_objects: Durable Objects (comes with Workers Scripts: Edit)

capabilities.account_read: Account Settings: Read (reads the account details)

github.title: Install the GitHub App

done.text: Your accounts are connected. Now pick a repository to create your first project.

done.agentReady: The agent is already set up and applies to all your projects.

newProject.lead: Pick a repository. bohr publishes the site to your Cloudflare account and sets up the agent's sandbox and the preview.
newProject.agentMissingTitle: The agent is not set up yet
newProject.agentMissing: Set up the provider and the key in your account settings. As soon as it is ready, the agent starts preparing the repository on its own.

source.repositoryHint: A GitHub repository you already have.

repository.installMore: Give access to more repositories on GitHub.

repository.branchHint: Approved changes are merged into this branch, and the production deploy starts from it.
repository.paymentRequired: Creating projects on bohr.io Cloud needs an active subscription.

template.text: bohr creates a GitHub repository from the template and a D1 database in your Cloudflare account, and publishes the site. Then ask the agent for changes like in any project.
template.name: Project name
template.nameHint: It is also the name of the GitHub repository: letters, numbers, “.”, “-” and “_”.
template.invalidName: Use only letters, numbers, “.”, “-” and “_” in the project name.
template.ownerHint: Where the repository is created on GitHub. The project runs in this owner's Cloudflare account.

provisioning.title: Setting up the project
provisioning.text: The instance is creating the project Worker, the agent sandbox and the preview. It usually takes a few minutes; keep this page open. Then the agent prepares the repository on its own.

bot.title: Create the project bot on Telegram
bot.text: With the bot, you and your team ask for changes and approve releases from Telegram. It is optional: the web chat works without it.
bot.skipHint: You can connect a bot later, in the project agent settings.

activation.text: This project came from the previous version of bohr and, for now, only publishes GitHub deploys. With the agent, you ask for changes in a conversation and approve each release.
activation.deployOnlyTitle: This project does not have the agent yet

activation.containersTitle: The agent needs the Workers Paid plan
activation.containersText: The site keeps deploying to your Cloudflare account. The agent's sandbox is a Cloudflare Container: the account needs the Workers Paid plan, and the token the Containers: Edit permission. Once it has them, check again.
activation.agentText: The project is ready, but the agent has no provider yet. Choose the provider and paste the key in your account settings: as soon as you save, the agent prepares the repository.

move.title: Hosted by bohr
move.text: This project came from the previous version of bohr and is still hosted in bohr's Cloudflare account. You can move it to your own account, where Cloud plan projects run.
move.how1: bohr opens a pull request in your repository that switches the deploy to your Cloudflare account, with the build settings and files it needs, and removes bohr v1's workflow.
move.how2: After the merge, GitHub Actions publishes the site in your account, and bohr copies the secrets and moves your domains.
move.how3: The bohr.io addresses start redirecting to the site's new address.
move.connectFirst: To continue, connect a Cloudflare account below.
move.confirmText: bohr will open a pull request that changes the deploy to the account {account}; the deploy gets its token from bohr, never from the repository. The site only changes after the merge.
move.cannotPrepare: The move could not be prepared automatically.
move.prepared: Pull request #{number} is open in your repository.
move.step1: Review and merge pull request #{number} on GitHub.
move.step2: Wait for the GitHub Actions deploy to finish.
move.step3: Come back here and click Finish the move.
move.notYet: It cannot be finished yet. Check that the pull request is merged and the GitHub Actions deploy has finished, then try again.
move.partial: Almost there: the site already runs in your account, but some domains still need you.
move.pendingHelp: For each pending domain, add the domain (its zone) to your Cloudflare account and point its nameservers to Cloudflare. Then click Finish the move again. Until then, the domain keeps showing the last version bohr published.
move.proxiedHelp: This domain's DNS stays with bohr (as in v1): bohr receives the requests and passes each one on to the Worker in your account. To have the DNS in your account, move the domain to your Cloudflare.
move.redirectedHelp: The bohr.io addresses now redirect to the site's new address.
move.droppedHelp: Branch preview addresses are no longer deployed.
move.done: Done! The project now runs in your Cloudflare account ({account}).

cliLogin.lead: The bohr CLI on a computer asked to sign in to your account. Approve it only if you just ran bohr login yourself.

setup.title: Set up the organization
setup.text: Like your account: the subscription, the Cloudflare account where the projects run and the agent. It applies to every project of the organization.
setup.subscriptionText: The organization has its own bohr.io Cloud subscription, paid by an admin. Members don't need a subscription to work on its projects.
setup.subscriptionPoint2: The projects run in the organization's Cloudflare account, connected in the next step.
setup.cloudflareText: The sites of the organization's projects and their domains are published to the organization's Cloudflare account. Any plan works, including the free one.
setup.agentText: The provider and key the agent uses in every project of the organization.

agent.noRuntime: The connection runs in the container of one of the organization's projects, and none is ready yet. Create a project first or use a token below.
agent.applied: Saved. None of the organization's projects is ready to receive them yet; new ones start with them. | Saved and applied to {count} project of the organization. | Saved and applied to {count} projects of the organization.
agent.removeText: The key is deleted and the agent is turned off in every project of the organization. GitHub deploys keep working.

members.title: Members
members.text: Members come from the GitHub organization: owners become admins, everyone else members.
members.permission: The GitHub app doesn't have the Members: read permission on this organization, so only the person who installed it was added. Grant Members: read to import the members and sync again.
members.pendingHint: Joins when they sign in to bohr with GitHub.
members.githubHint: GitHub is the source of the members: removing someone here takes away their access in bohr without changing GitHub. Roles changed here last until the role changes on GitHub.
members.removeText: {login} loses access to the organization's projects in bohr. They stay in the GitHub organization, and syncing doesn't bring the access back.
members.lastAdmin: The organization needs at least one admin. Make someone else an admin first.

settings.adminsOnly: Only the organization's admins change its settings.
settings.name: Name
settings.nameHint: The name and picture come from the GitHub organization.
settings.cloudflareText: The organization's projects run in this Cloudflare account.
settings.cloudflareConfirmText: bohr forgets the token of the {name} account. Not possible while projects of the organization run there.
settings.agentText: The agent's provider, key, model and effort in every project of the organization.
settings.billingActive: The organization's bohr.io Cloud subscription is active.
settings.billingNone: The organization has no subscription. bohr.io Cloud costs {price} per month per organization.

delete.title: Danger zone
delete.text: Deleting the organization removes its projects from bohr, and everything bohr created for them. The GitHub repositories aren't changed.
delete.projects: The organization's projects are deleted (agents, previews, bots and bohr routes).
delete.subscription: The organization's subscription is canceled, and its Cloudflare accounts and agent are disconnected.
delete.github: The bohr app is uninstalled from the GitHub organization. The repositories aren't changed.
delete.sitesStay: The sites published in the organization's Cloudflare account stay online.
delete.deleteSites: Also delete the sites published in the organization's Cloudflare account
delete.deleteSitesHint: Removes each site's production Worker and the deploy secrets of the repositories.
delete.warnings: The organization was deleted, but something was left behind: {list}

new.title: New organization
new.lead: A bohr organization is a GitHub organization with the bohr app installed: its members come from GitHub, and it has its own subscription, Cloudflare account and agent.
new.step1: If you don't have one yet, create it on GitHub. You need to be an owner to install the app.
new.step2Title: Install the bohr app on it
new.step2: On GitHub, pick the organization and the repositories bohr can access. Then GitHub brings you back to the organization’s page.
new.members: bohr imports the organization's members with the matching role: owners become admins, everyone else members.
new.install: Install the GitHub app on an organization
new.installError: The organization could not be created: {detail}

newProject.lead: Pick one of the organization's repositories. bohr publishes the site to the organization's Cloudflare account and sets up the agent's sandbox and the preview.
newProject.agentMissingAdmin: Set the provider and key in the organization's settings. Once it's ready, the agent starts preparing the repository on its own.
newProject.agentMissing: An admin of the organization needs to set up the agent. Until then, the project only publishes what reaches GitHub.
newProject.paymentRequired: The organization needs an active subscription. An admin can subscribe on the organization's page.

dns.title: Domains
dns.lead: Domains whose DNS bohr hosts: bohr v1 kept them in bohr's Cloudflare account. Manage their records here: email, verifications, your own servers.
dns.none: You have no domains whose DNS bohr hosts.
dns.guide: How to move a domain to your own Cloudflare account

zone.title: Domain
zone.lead: The DNS records of {name}, in bohr's Cloudflare account. Changes apply right away.
zone.readOnly: You can see these records. Only the domain's owner or an admin of {org} can change them.
zone.adminNotice: You are changing someone else's domain as an instance admin. Each change goes to the audit log.
zone.empty: This domain has no DNS records.
zone.lockedHint: Records marked “Used by bohr” send this domain's sites to bohr (or are its nameservers) and can't be changed here. Everything else is yours to change.

dns.usedByBohrTitle: bohr uses this record to serve a site, or it is one of the domain's nameservers.

dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHint: Use {'@'} for {zone} itself, or a subdomain like www.
dialog.proxiedHint: Traffic goes through Cloudflare (HTTPS, cache, protection) and the server's address stays hidden. Leave it off for mail and other services that are not websites.
dialog.priorityRequired: MX and SRV records need a priority from 0 to 65535.
